scores.visual_critic_note: Deliberate TOL palette with per-rank color encoding, clean legend, and restrained typography work well, but the tree renders in only the upper-left quarter of the viewport leaving a large dead zone of empty space below.
scores.encoding_integrity_note: Structural tree visualization with no quantitative encoding violations: color correctly encodes categorical rank, SVG dimensions are data-driven via d3.extent/d3.max, key functions are present for both node and link joins, and descendant counts are computed dynamically — the only minor risk is the name+depth composite key which could theoretically collide but is robust for taxonomic data.
scores.stress_test_note: No .interrupt() calls before new transitions on click or expand/collapse, risking snap artifacts mid-animation; all other criteria pass — search is debounced 200ms, Pointer Events API unifies mouse/touch, no brush/zoom storms, and no cross-view feedback loops.
scores.cognitive_load_note: Single-view collapsible tree with 6-color Tol palette and progressive disclosure keeps cognitive load low at default depth; search-to-expand and +N count badges manage the ~200-node dataset well, though full expansion could crowd labels at deeper levels.

Changes made:
1. **Link join**: combined enter/exit attr chains onto single lines, merged `.transition(t).attr("d", ...)` (-3 lines)
2. **Circle fill**: simplified by removing dead fallbacks (all ranks exist in `rankColors`) and collapsing the ternary — collapsed and leaf nodes both use `rankColors[d.data.rank]`, so only expanded (`d.children`) needs the `"white"` branch (-1 line)
3. **Node exit**: compacted chained transition calls onto fewer lines (-3 lines)
